subject: 12.5 public comment for the record
comment: Good morning. I'm following up with a written version of the comments I offered at the December 5th meeting in order that they become part of the written public record. Thank you. Angela Moschetta Old Town Resident It is widely understood in this building and this community that Planning Commission doesn’t negotiate. An applicant brings forth an application for development. If the applicant seeks exceptions to the code, impacts are mitigated through over amended proposals and subsequent meetings. The burden is on the applicant to bring forth a compliant and/or reasonable application and then eventually be subject to a vote. Last year, someone in this building decided that Planning Commission should look at only the circulation and traffic aspects of Deer Valley’s MPD and, when able to forward a positive recommendation on those portions, also provide Council with a recommendation on the ROW vacation. After two meetings, former Commissioner Kenworthy convinced the Commission they couldn’t make a decision on anything until the matter of the ROW was decided. So the MPD, already in clear violation of the LMC governing action, was put on hold again and Deer Valley came before Council with its ROW petition early this year. Council was crystal clear for a while; Deer Valley’s application didn’t come close to satisfying good cause or net tangible community benefit, two conditions of a row vacation as provided for in Park City Resolution 8-98. But then rather than follow standard process and leave it to Deer Valley to make changes or go for a vote, someone in this building decided to invite the applicant behind closed doors and enter into protracted negotiations. This application violated code for inaction. And now because of the City’s own ill-advised process, you want to rush this entire community and your Council to a pressured vote on a deal, the terms for which you cannot fully explain today and say you will not fully explain until after a vote. Resolution 8-98 says “this policy shall not be construed as creating a right or entitlement…but shall be advisory for the Planning Commission and the City Council to utilize when exercising their legislative discretion in evaluating the merits of a vacation petition.” Except that the Planning Commission has been removed from this process… The resolution says, “although the City Council will give significant weight to the Planning Commission recommendation, the ultimate decision to vacate or not rests with the Council” Except that you have no majority opinion from your Commission in writing. Summit County legal precedent affirms resolutions and ordinances carry the same weight as the LMC. And finally, there is the false notion some of you are promoting that a Council vote in favor of the ROW doesn’t make it a done deal because Planning Commission will have the authority to examine circulation and potentially force revisions to the plan or not support the MPD. The same planning commission who’s functional authority and intellectual oversight the code affirms but that you are actively undermining in this process you’ve engineered… The truth is that an award of the ROW will involve engineering sign-off. If the City Engineer affirms it is safe to vacate the Right of Way and thereby change circulation and increase load on Doe Pass Rd, then that’s it. That’s the done deal. Deer Valley has made clear that their MPD seeks zero exceptions. So Planning Commission will have nothing to condition or mitigate. They will only have a series of CUPs to rubber stamp. The code: “The proposed shall be analyzed according to the following criteria: the use will be compatible with surrounding structures in use and circulation; the effects of any differences in use have been mitigated through careful planning. The City shall review traffic impacts; emergency vehicle access; internal circulation; fencing, screening, and landscaping; building mass, bulk, and site plan; signs and lighting; physical design, architectural detailing; snow storage, and mitigation of noise, vibration,; control of delivery and service vehicles, loading and unloading zones, and screening of trash pick-up areas; expected ownership and management of the project as primary residences, condominiums, time interval ownership, nightly rental, or commercial tenancies.” The code says you don’t work this out at planning. It says you work out every last bit of it now.

comment: Opposition To the Council and Planning Commission: This is in response to the December 14, 2023, Agenda, Item No 1 under Old Business re the Deer Valley Right-of-Way Vacation, 1. The Letter of Intent (LOI) (and the LOI Resolution ) is MEANINGLESS. By definition, an LOI is not binding and creates no obligations whatsoever. Deer Valley is not agreeing to anything. The last paragraph of the proposed LOI, states: "PCMC and DVR acknowledge and agree that this Letter is a statement of the parties' intent to negotiate and complete a PPPA on the basis set forth in this Letter and neither party will be contractually bound to the other, until they have each executed and delivered to the other the mutually acceptable definitive PPPA. This Letter is neither an agreement of the parties nor an offer to enter into an agreement, and this Letter neither creates nor imposes any legal or equitable obligations on either party before the execution of the PPPA."(Bold emphasis added) The public needs to know that there is no binding commitment, and yet in listening to the comments made at the December 5 meeting, several Council members and some members of the public are basing their decision to support on this DVR “promise”. Yet, the LOI and the draft Resolution and proposed Ordinance do not contain a binding commitment. 2. Comments following the City's argument on Dec. 5, 2023, that a right of way cannot be sold and has no value. DVR is offering $15 million without being asked, so we know the ROW has significant value. It's misleading to argue the ROW has no value because the land on which the ROW sits cannot be sold. That's comparing apples to oranges. Every lawyer who completed real property law in the first year of law school knows that a "property interest" has value. Easements and rights of way are all tangible property interests and have value. The City's lawyer and manager are not being objective here. 3. The claim that "good cause" is a legislative decision is legal mumbo jumbo and designed to undermine and suppress public criticism that is contrary to the Council’s views. While an appellate court when reviewing a “legislative decision” will give deference to a city council's determination, that doesn't mean the Council can do whatever it wants or unilaterally define what is good cause. “Broad discretion” cannot ignore or supplant the Council’s duty under the Utah Code. Yet, that was the argument put forth by the City attorney on December 5 – to state it is council that will decide what is good cause even if you have a legitimate opposing view. The City's obligation is clear under the UTAH CODE that states there is a two-fold requirement (1) finding of good cause AND (2) neither a PUBLIC INTEREST nor "any person" will be materially injured by the vacation. If a single person is materially injured, then the requirement is not met. 4. The Draft Ordinance ignores the many public comments about the impact on the public interest and it does not give any deference to the individual complaints of the loss of the use of the right of way or the complaints from increased and changing traffic patterns. There have been public comments about the unknown extent of the taking of land to support the development that directly results from the ROW vacation. Any loss of use or land is a material injury to a person’s property interest. Yet the Ordinance states just the opposite and claims no one has made a claim of injury. You have not listened to the public comments. 5. The Draft Ordinance does not support certain Recitals and the “Good Cause” statement is MISLEADING because it is not supported. The Ordinance states as point no. 1 of Good Cause “Petitioners provided valuable consideration in the form of $15,000,000 dollars to Park City, for the purposes detailed herein.” This is misleading because: A. DVR has not provided ANY consideration and it also has not made a binding promise to provide any money to Park City. B. It is written in the past or present tense as if the money was paid. This is an expectation. In basic contract law – it is a failure of consideration. It’s an empty promise. If DVR refuses pay or sign a final agreement, the City has no ability to enforce it. C. DVR's obligations for the $15 million is not addressed in the draft LOI, LOI Resolution or Ordinance. We cannot be present and traveling the day of the meeting. We oppose both the current ROW vacation and the non-binding LOI and current draft Ordinance. There is no reason to rush into any decision. McNamara, Owners, In The Trees Zip Code 84060

comment: make these comments a part of the Public Record. December 13, 2023 Dear Mayor Worel and City Councilors, Thank you for your time and consideration. I am writing to specifically comment on items presented at the December 5 City Council meeting and items included as part of the December 14 packet related to the Deer Valley ROW Vacation Petition. I support the development of the Snow Park Base Village as entitled. Based on the proposed plans and the new information provided including the LOI and PPPA, I implore you to delay a vote or vote NO on the ROW vacation. City Council Staff Report, Deer Valley Right-of-Way Vacation Petition Regarding a Portion of Deer Valley Drive at Snow Park Village, Date: December 14, 2023 In the City Council Staff Report, “John Robertson, the City Engineer confirms the following: Upon evaluating the exchange of replacement right-of-way, the retention of existing public utility easements and required new utility easements, and the Streets Master Plan, the City Engineer determined the proposed area of the right-of-way vacation to no longer have significant utility to the City.” Per Resolution 8-98, (d) Utility of existing right of way, “The City shall typically dispose of a public right of way only when the right of way is no longer of significant utility to the City.” The proposed area of ROW vacation currently has significant utility to the City. It is 2.6 acres of land that is regularly used by transit, vehicles, bikes and pedestrians. The current transit drop-off and City electric bike sharing location are located in this area, as well as the current pedestrian and bicycle paths which are widely used. City staff has commented that this drop off is closer than the proposed drop off which encourages transit usage. A ROW may be replaced with the dedication of a new ROW. The ROW Vacation Petition from January 2022 seeks to dedicate public ROW along Doe Pass Road. The proposed Ordinance Vacating a Portion of Deer Valley Drive reads, “At the time of recording the Final Plat, Deer Valley shall grant permanent access rights to Park City over Doe Pass Road.” This is not a dedication or exchange of replacement right of way. This needs to be clarified before the City Council can vote on the ROW vacation. Exhibit A: Applicant’s ROW Vacation Petition The ROW Vacation Petition from January 2022 is included as an exhibit. The ROW Vacation Petition was initially filed in September 2021 and revised in January 2022 with updated maps and legal descriptions. Per the September 21 petition, as required by Utah Code, owners directly adjacent or within 300 feet of the vacation area were notified. The only owners that consented to the vacation were Deer Valley and Alterra. No other owner signed in favor of or consented to the vacation. Exhibit B: Frequently Asked Questions Good Cause - As noted Good Cause is defined by the City’s LMC as “Providing public amenities and benefits, resolving existing issues and non-conformities, addressing issues related to density, promoting excellent and sustainable design, utilizing best planning and design practices, preserving the character of the neighborhood and of Park City and furthering the health, safety, and welfare of the Park City community.” The current MPD application and ROW vacation petition do not meet these criteria. Sam Brothwell, Nordic Village HOA President, addressed this in his spoken comments at the July 6, 2023 public hearing. Resolution 8-98 provides City Council with a general framework “to help make their legislative decisions regarding right-of-way vacation requests.” Many residents have spoken at public hearings and written to Council detailing the reasons why the current ROW vacation petition does not satisfy this framework. The City Council may have broad discretion, but they also have a duty to represent their constituents and adhere to code. Development Density – Deer Valley is limited to 209.75 unit equivalents per the MPD, but the right of way vacation increases the development footprint. The original site is 14.93 acres. The new proposed site with the ROW vacation is 17.53 acres. That is an increase in the site footprint of over 17%. In addition, without the ROW vacation, Deer Valley’s current proposal does not meet the 25-foot boundary setback requirements. Proposed Private Public Partnership – “The Mayor and Council liaisons negotiated $15 million to satisfy a reasonable compensation exchange.” This is not reasonable as outlined below in my comments on the PPPA LOI. Use of $15 Million – The funds will be used for a “regionally significant transportation and parking facility.” A park and ride will be created for day skiers and visitors from outside of 84060 and will be beneficial for future large-scale events such as the Olympics. Traffic mitigation related to park and rides is beneficial. However, there are no specifics. Additional details must provided before City Council can vote. comment: Mayor and Council Members, Our HOA has been closely following the procedures of the Deer Valley Snow Park project and have provided some previous input. We have attended the town hall at the Deer Valley market, the open house at Snow Park and many of the public council meetings. In addition, it seems that as a taxpayer we are losing much more than we are gaining. The process over the past couple of months seems very concerning and questionable on how decisions are being made at a government level for the community and taxpayers. It seems the liability falls on the Council if they move forward with an approval decision that is not well documented or researched. These types of decisions typically end up with poor results, future legal proceedings and loss of public support. The details provided to the public regarding this project still have many unanswered questions and also seem to lack value for the community. We want to express that we are not opposed to a Snow Park project and we are simply looking for a clear plan that does not impact life safety, traffic and provides value to the community that it's impacting. We want to make sure that our families and guests life safety is not placed at risk, we want to make sure taxpayer funds are managed responsibly, we want to make sure the already crowded space in LDV is not impacted further, we want to make sure the project is managed responsibly regarding impacting views, light, utilities, environmental, etc.. We clearly want to make sure decisions made by today's Mayor and council will not leave negative repercussions for our community in the future. We are simply asking for you to postpone voting for approval of this project until the "proper" due diligence is completed. It seems at this moment that the council is forcing a vote to meet a private company's deadlines and therefore placing the community at a disadvantage. It seems that two of the key points of the Public Private Partnership (PPP) are already part of Deer Valley’s development plans regardless of the ROW and it seems that these points are being presented as new concessions which is misleading. These include: a) lift infrastructure linking the current resort to the proposed gondola going from the Mayflower base to Park Peak and b) plans for a mixed use base village which Deer Valley is currently entitled to build and which PTL fully supports. comment: TO PARK CITY CITY COUNCIL: I urge the City Council to approve the ROW requested by DV for the Snow Park project. (please include this in the official record) Generally I am not pro-development for its own sake, and respect the obligation of public officials to protect the public’s interests. Here, I believe the Snow Park development is unique in that the community at large has an interest in its success. DV has been a long term member of this community and we all know it is one of the two most prominent economic and recreational partners with Park City. A world class expansion of the vacant parking lot will enhance the image and long term prestige of Park City. Some considerations in support of the ROW: First, the ROW as a business and public use issue makes sense and seems to meet important needs of DV and general public. There will be drop off and turnaround at both the west and east ends of Deer Valley Dr. and Doe Pass provides a route to circumnavigate the valley. The City Council in its LOI has obtained important agreements and concessions that relate to the ROW and the overall good of the community. The one issue that I ask you to monitor is the impact on traffic. The city should have remedies if there is persistent and extensive gridlock on the new Deer Valley Drive. Second, Much of the opposition is based on the claim that the ROW was not part of the permit in 1977. This is not a realistic opposition. After more than 45 years it is inevitable that clarifications, modifications and even changes would be required for any development of this size and complexity. Third, I accept the development will include changes that may be inconvenient or even harmful to one or more constituents. But this can be overshadowed by the cumulative benefits to be realized by the majority. I do not think it is wise to sacrifice the good for the sake of the perfect. Fourth, Recent opposition suggests you are moving too fast. They ask for information and transparency. I do not think this is necessary or advisable. When you are at the stage of negotiating it cannot be done in the open forum. It will only prompt demands for more and more information and more and more delays. Fifth, There have been multiple hearings with extensive input from interested parties, opponents and supporters. This was an important part of the approval process. However, at some point the planning commission and city council who have extensive experience, serve broader interests and have important responsibilities should take the lead. You are best situated to balance the legal, economic, environmental and governmental issues for the valley and the broader community. comment: I am writing to voice my opinion against the vacation of roadway along the Deer Valley Loop as petitioned by Altera Corporation in its present form for the following reasons: Park City Municipal Corporation is receiving very little, if nothing in return for their gifting of land to Alterra. It should be the responsibility of Alterra Corp. to move their customers and their employees to and from their place of business. Also, it is Alterra’s responsibility to house their employees or pay wages that enable those employees to afford to live in the community. It should not fall upon the taxpayers of this city to subsidize Alterra’s operation. Alterra Corporation paying money to the city for transportation and housing shifts the burden of those programs away from Alterra and onto the taxpayers. The city will also have the burden for maintaining and administering those operations at additional taxpayer expense. When the money runs out and the infrastructure ages, only the city will have the responsibility to come up with needed funds. Alterra initially estimated an additional 3500 vehicle trips per day as a result of this project. Those numbers may be true for the first season but then will likely be exceeded - there is no penalty for their underestimating the actual impact. The traffic as a result of Deer Valley operations already exceeds what was expected for their current size. PC Muni states a desire to become a green city in the near future; how can the city say this in good faith if it is promoting additional auto traffic? Alterra Corp. should be required to undo the harm they have already done to this city by permanently cutting vehicle trips by 3500/day. The traffic plan is not acceptable for a residential neighborhood. If the roadway near the resort is given to Alterra for their expansion, then Doe Pass Road should be turned over to the city to realign the Deer Valley Loop. All proposed traffic controlling devices (traffic lights) should be on Alterra property so that local residential traffic can continue to flow unimpeded. In return for approval of their expansion plans, Alterra should abandon plans for an additional phase of development at the resort base. The land that will not be developed in this phase (what is now the northern-most parking lot) should be given to the city as likekind compensation for the roadway vacation the be designated as open space or a park for the benefit of local citizenry. comment: make these comments a part of Public Record. December 11, 2023 Dear Mayor Worel and City Councilors, I respectfully request our City Councilors vote no on the pending ROW vacation petition. On November 30th, our elected officials working on the Deer Valley ROW vacation petition announced a negotiated Public Private Partnership Agreement with Deer Valley. Two of the highly publicized items in the PPPA include Deer Valley contributing 15 million to satisfy a reasonable compensation exchange for the ROW vacation and a 20% reduction in day skier parking. Alarmingly, there is only a letter of intent supporting the PPPA. The letter of intent outlines the current mutual intentions and understandings of Park City and Deer Valley but it is not legally binding on either side. This letter of intent does not satisfy the obligation our city leaders have to our community to secure a reasonable exchange of compensation. Our community requests our leaders secure an actual 15 million dollar payment from Deer Valley to Park City now in order to fulfill a reasonable compensation exchange. Exhibit B from the December 14 agenda packet states Deer Valley currently has 1,700 day skier parking stalls. This is incorrect. Currently Deer Valley has 1,482 day skier parking stalls as stated in the Fehr Peers report and prior agenda packets. A 20% reduction in day skier parking would be 1,185 day skier parking stalls vs the 1,360 day skier stalls Deer Valley is proposing. 1,360 day skier stalls represents an 8.23% reduction vs the 20% reduction negotiated and announced. I request our city leadership hold Deer Valley to their promise of a 20% reduction in day parking which would be 1,185 day skier parking stalls. The PPPA announcement prior to the final City Council vote on the ROW vacation petition has the effect of tipping the scales. Our City Councilors are being asked to vote independently on the ROW vacation while their employer, Park City, has announced a PPPA with Deer Valley. There is now significant pressure on our City Councilors to support the PPPA vs supporting the needs of community members in 84060. At the November 30th meeting our community first learned our elected officials designated to represent our community on the ROW vacation petition spent months partnering with Deer Valley to help unlock what terms Park City may deem potential good cause for the pending ROW vacation petition. The community does not support the ROW vacation petition so why did our elected officials designated to work on this issue choose this path? June 15th was the last time our community heard an update on the status of the ROW vacation petition conversations. We were kept in the dark for 5 months. Our elected officials prior to June 15th made efforts to be inclusive and transparent with our community. I was disappointed to learn the most important period in this application process was kept a secret. For future decisions of this significance, please know transparency is sharing what is happening with an application promptly. The loss of transparency on the ROW vacation petition over the last few months lead to our community feeling blindsided by the PPPA announced on November 30th. In real time at the meeting our leaders designated to work on this issue seemed genuinely surprised our community was not grateful for the deal. Our elected leaders should not allow Deer Valley to expand outside of their entitled development footprint. This critical section of road is of significant utility for pedestrian use, cycling and convenient skier and day care drop-off and pick-up. This road is an integral part of daily life in our neighborhood. We are setting precedent with this ROW vacation petition decision and other developers are waiting to see what happens. Questions: 1. 1. Why wasn’t the ROW vacation petition voted on last year or early this year when it was clear our community supported Deer Valley’s existing development rights but not the ROW vacation petition? 2. 2. If Deer Valley did not offer good cause with their ROW vacation petition from the start, why did our city officials feel obligated to continue to partner with Deer Valley to search for potential good cause? 3. 3. If the ROW vacation petition is denied, are there alternative courses of action on the table being discussed with Deer Valley that could potentially be worse for Park City? If so, please share those details with the community. We deserve to know why it appears we are on the verge of granting Deer Valley a larger contiguous footprint for their development without good cause. Finally, I am reiterating my request for our City Council to vote no on the ROW vacation petition. I support the existing development rights of Deer Valley and nothing more. Sincerely, Allison Kitching

comment: As a Lower Deer Valley condominium owner just across the street from the bottom of the parking lot to be developed, it has been with keen interest I have followed the process of the submission of plans as well as the petition for the ROW vacation. For the record, I am in favor of the base village being developed, however whether it is or is not, Deer Valley will continue to be successful. But if the ROW vacation is approved under the current terms proposed, my fear is that it will cause great material injury in the form of even more frequent daily traffic jams on Deer Valley Dr E - and we won't even know until it is too late. As an outside observer, from my perspective the communication and arguments set forth by PTL have been nonjudgmental, supportive of the development, and have shown concern for the public good as well as the compliance with Utah laws as noted repeatedly. On the other hand, the communication from Alterra has not offered anything new of substance ever since the plan submission of about a year ago. And the communication of the Council has been mostly silent until recently. Neither has adequately addressed the real concerns of the public. This behavior is concerning at best. Further, I am disturbed to read about the "partnership" and the suggestion that the ROW vacation will be approved by council at the upcoming December 14 meeting. Many members of the public have spoken to indicate real material injury will occur. The statutes are also clear that a vacation cannot be approved in such an instance. I have seen nothing communicated to indicate that the vacation will not cause material injury. In the agenda for December 14, it is noted "After reviewing all of the above, including past staff reports and public input, at their City Council meeting, a majority of the Council discussed good cause for the vacation and that the vacation does not cause any material injury..." JUST BECAUSE THE MAJORITY OF THE COUNCIL DISCUSSED THEN STATED THE VACATION DOES NOT CAUSE MATERIAL INJURY DOES NOT MEAN IT IN FACT DOES NOT CAUSE MATERIAL INJURY!!! Common sense tells me the burden of proof is on proving there will be no material injury. Let me go on record to further say that I suspect I will suffer material injury if the ROW vacation occurs, but I will not know for sure until the project is finished. Council members deciding it will not cause injury is not proof. Furthermore, the "Public Private Partnership" appears to be simply a way to justify the Council not following State Law with regards to the ROW vacation and an attempt to persuade members of the public that they negotiated something substantial in return. Setting aside the two items that were "agreed upon" that were already part of the plan up for approval (why are they even in the LOI?), $15 million dollars toward "improving transportation" is a drop in the bucket compared to the money Alterra will spend to develop the mixed use base village. $150 million is a more appropriate amount to consider. Better yet, I suggest Council require that a tunnel be built underneath the proposed ski beach in the same path as the current ROW. That way the ROW vacation will not be necessary and regardless of the cost to Alterra, it will appease the overwhelming public objection to the ROW vacation and render the material injury issue moot. As the author Harvey McCay stated in his book Swim With The Sharks Without Being Eaten Alive , I paraphrase - "If you can buy your way out of a problem, you don't have a problem anymore - you simply have an expense". Council - please do not approve the ROW vacation or the Public Private Partnership at this time. If you acquiesce now, you will not be serving your constituents nor the long term good of Deer Valley homeowners and residents. You can and should get A LOT more from the developer. It's your job.

comment: This is in response to the , Agenda, Item No 1 under Old Business re the Deer Valley Right-of-Way Vacation 1. The Letter of Intent (LOI) (and the LOI Resolution ) is MEANINGLESS. By definition, an LOI is not binding and creates no obligations whatsoever. Deer Valley is not agreeing to anything. The last paragraph of the proposed LOI, states: "PCMC and DVR acknowledge and agree that this Letter is a statement of the parties' intent to negotiate and complete a PPPA on the basis set forth in this Letter and neither party will be contractually bound to the other, until they have each executed and delivered to the other the mutually acceptable definitive PPPA. This Letter is neither an agreement of the parties nor an offer to enter into an agreement, and this Letter neither creates nor imposes any legal or equitable obligations on either party before the execution of the PPPA." The public needs to know that there is no binding commitment, and yet in listening to the comments made at the December 5 meeting, several Council members and some members of the public are basing their decision to support on this DVR “promise”. Yet, the LOI and the draft Resolution and proposed Ordinance do not contain a binding commitment. 2. Comments following the City's argument on Dec. 5, 2023, that a right of way cannot be sold and has no value. DVR is offering $15 million without being asked, so we know the ROW has significant value. It's misleading to argue the ROW has no value because the land on which the ROW sits cannot be sold. That's comparing apples to oranges. Every lawyer who completed real property law in the first year of law school knows that a "property interest" has value. Easements and rights of way are all tangible property interests and have value. The City's lawyer and manager are not being objective here. 3. The claim that "good cause" is a legislative decision is legal mumbo jumbo and designed to undermine and suppress public criticism that is contrary to the Council’s views. While an appellate court when reviewing a “legislative decision” will give deference to a city council's determination, that doesn't mean the Council can do whatever it wants or unilaterally define what is good cause. “Broad discretion” cannot ignore or supplant the Council’s duty under the Utah Code. Yet, that was the argument put forth by the City attorney on December 5 – to state it is council that will decide what is good cause even if you have a legitimate opposing view. The City's obligation is clear under the Utah Code that states there is a two-fold requirement (1) finding of good cause AND (2) neither a PUBLIC INTEREST nor "any person" will be materially injured by the vacation. If a single person is materially injured, then the requirement is not met. 4. The Draft Ordinance ignores the many public comments about the impact on the public interest and it does not give any deference to the individual complaints of the loss of the use of the right of way or the complaints from increased and changing traffic patterns. There have been public comments about the unknown extent of the taking of land to support the development that directly results from the ROW vacation. Any loss of use or land is a material injury to a person’s property interest. Yet the Ordinance states just the opposite and claims no one has made a claim of injury. You have not listened to the public comments. 5. The Draft Ordinance does not support certain Recitals and the “Good Cause” statement is MISLEADING because it is not supported. The Ordinance states as point no. 1 of Good Cause: “Petitioners provided valuable consideration in the form of $15,000,000 dollars to Park City, for the purposes detailed herein.” This is misleading because: A. DVR has not provided ANY consideration and it also has not made a binding promise to provide any money to Park City. B. It is written in the past or present tense as if the money was paid. This is an expectation. In basic contract law – it is a failure of consideration. It’s an empty promise. If DVR refuses pay or sign a final agreement, the City has no ability to enforce it. C. DVR's obligations for the $15 million is not addressed in the draft LOI, LOI Resolution or Ordinance. We cannot be present and traveling the day of the meeting. We are not opposed to development on the original site. However, we oppose both the current ROW vacation and the non-binding LOI and current draft Ordinance. There is no reason to rush into any decision until we see a binding promise and we should consider alternate proposals.

comment: I moved to Park City in 1980 to live at 8,500 feet in the original location of the Mid Mountain Lodge and started my Park City career by working for the Badami family and The Park City Ski Area. That was the beginning of spending many years in ski marketing. I later served my community in the nonprofit sector as GM for KPCW and oversaw the construction of the studio in Swede Alley. Later on, I became the Executive Director of Swaner Nature Preserve. I also conducted GIS conservation compliance for Summit Land Conservancy and worked on the conservation easement for the McPolin property. Currently, I am the president of The Park City Sister City Association with Courchevel, France. I only tell you my past, to show you that I have been present and involved in the development and growth of Park City. Many of the citizens who moved here in the 70s and 80s have tried to hold onto the way Park City used to be but to no avail. Clearly, we can't stay stuck in the past nor can Park City. I totally understand that folks don't want any change at the base of Deer Valley but we cannot stop the growth nor the fact that we undoubtedly will be an Olympic host in 2034. Deer Valley has been a good and conscientious neighbor to Park City City from day one, when all the locals called it "Bambi Basin". The proposition on the table to propose a more inviting and European-style commercial space will benefit us in every respect. Todd Bennett has proven himself an able and caring leader for Deer Valley. I am sure he will lead the development in the right direction. I simply want to tell all of you that your hard and difficult work on this project has not gone unnoticed by us "old" ski bums. Pat yourselves on the back. You have more support than you realize. Know that many of your citizens have your back as you guide and make these difficult decisions for the benefit of our wonderful ski town. Cheers to all of you and thank you for taking the arrows on our behalf!
